Subject: Post-call recap — concurrency handshake and live-surge qualification

Emma — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same mental model going into the demonstration: 

1) Goals you stated on the call
- Support peak retail-hour bursts up to ~2,000 concurrent requests for short windows (2–7 minutes).
- Maintain 95th percentile tail latency <= 200 ms for streaming responses when model outputs exceed 256 tokens.
- Target steady-state concurrency ~800 for daytime traffic with occasional fan-out to >1k.

2) Redwood qualification asks (what we need to validate during the demo/test)
- Representative QPS and concurrency profile (CSV): 1-minute buckets for a 24h period + annotated surge windows.
- Acceptable maximum queue depth and max waiting time before backpressure/fallback.
- Any streaming-specific requirements (interleaved token delivery, chunk size, connection timeouts).

3) Proposed Redwood approach for the qualification exercise
- Warm pool seeding: maintain a warm pool sized for 25% of target burst (initial suggestion: 200 warm workers for your expected 800->2,000 spike).
- Fast-scale path: cold-start path limited to a 30s scale-up target for the first extra capacity tranche; subsequent scale increments targeted at <12s.
- Queueing behavior: token-bucket-based ingress with a hard queue cap; when queue > X we’ll auto-failover to a lower-cost model variant to preserve tail latency.
- Streaming: preserve incremental token delivery while priming KV cache so early tokens are low-latency — this will be part of the test.

4) Action items (owners)
- ParcelFlow (Emma): share sample 24h traffic csv + callouts for two example surge windows (due: Wed 2028-10-10).
- Redwood (Jonas): circulate a short SLO matrix spreadsheet and diagram of warm-pool priming that maps to your numbers (attachment: slo_matrix.xlsx, warmup-diagram.png) (due: Tue 2028-10-09).
- Redwood (Marissa/Vivek): prepare a scoped demo that includes a 5-minute controlled surge, streaming token checks, and queueing fallbacks (demo slots: Thu 2028-10-11 or Fri 2028-10-12).
- ParcelFlow SRE: confirm whether connections are long-lived WebSocket-style or short-lived HTTP streaming (affects priming strategy).

5) Risks and notes
- If peak bursts exceed the warm pool sizing assumptions, the cold-start tail for the first additional workers could exceed the scale-up target; we’ll show a fallback pattern during the demo.
- For streaming workloads the KV cache warm time matters — we’ll instrument that during the smoke-run and show token-by-token latencies.

Please reply with the CSV and your preferred demo slot. If anything above is incorrect or missing, call it out and I’ll update the doc.

— Jonas
